Definition: a height (as a seat of idolatry)
BiblicalUsage: Ramah is a height — a high place, a seat of idolatry. Ezekiel says to Jerusalem, 'thou hast also built unto thee an eminent place, and hast made thee an high place in every street,' and at the head of every way she built her high place.
TheologicalSignificance: What strikes me is that the high place is the heart's own altar: Jerusalem built one in every street, and God calls it what it is — whoredom against Him.
Sources: Strong's Exhaustive Concordance (1890), via OpenScriptures Strong's Dictionary (CC BY-SA)
